zh.summary: 把風險管理、事件應變與法遵串成持續改善的決策循環；從生活案例學會分辨事實、假設與責任。

sourceBody.text: Risk Management · Incident Response · Laws & Standards
Module 01：Introduction to Ethical Hacking（道德駭客入門）
這是 CEH M01 的最後一個學習單元。我們要把前面六堂課的知識串起來，理解一個組織如何真正做好資訊安全。
一、先掌握全貌：資訊安全是一套持續運作的管理系統
本堂課最重要的結論：
資安不是發現漏洞就修補、出現警報就關閉，而是持續判斷風險、採取行動、驗證結果，並改善下一次的決策。
你可以先把整堂課想成三個問題：

rows: 事情還沒發生，先決定怎麼預防
哪些風險最值得優先處理？
事情可能已經發生，開始查證與處理
發生什麼事？如何避免傷害擴大？
確認規則、責任與適用要求
我們應該遵守什麼？誰必須負責？

sourceBody.text: 補充查證：本表為了入門先從事前預防理解風險管理；事件處理中與事後仍要持續評估風險，不是等下一次事件才重新開始。[NIST 事件應變](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/incident-response)
另外還有一個貫穿全程的觀念：
Continuous Improvement（持續改善）：利用每次檢查、演練與事件的經驗，改善未來的防護與管理。
以下用四張 SVG 圖解，逐步建立這些概念之間的關係。
SVG 圖解 ①｜資安管理的完整決策循環

sourceBody.alt: 資安管理的完整決策循環。風險管理 Risk Management：確認重要資產與威脅，評估可能性、影響及現有控制，決定優先順序與複查時間。 事件應變 Incident Response：查核告警與原始證據，依授權圍堵、處理原因並驗證復原，不憑猜測結案。 改善治理 Continuous Improvement：找出偵測與流程缺口，更新權限、制度、演練及訓練。 回到風險管理：用事後經驗重新評估殘餘風險。修好漏洞不等於管理完所有風險；關閉告警不等於確認沒事。
sourceBody.caption: 資安管理的完整決策循環｜原始 SVG，圖中文字維持原樣。

sourceBody.text: 請沿著圖中的箭頭閱讀：
風險管理 → 事件應變 → 改善治理 → 回到風險管理。
例如，一間醫院發現自己的病歷系統存在安全問題：
平常，資安團隊會評估病歷可能外洩的風險，並安排存取權限控管。某天，如果出現不正常的大量下載，資安團隊就必須調查，確認是否涉及未授權存取。
即使事件處理完畢，工作仍然沒有結束。
團隊還要追問：為什麼原本的權限控管沒有阻止這個問題？偵測機制是否太慢？是否應該修改制度？
這些答案又會影響下一輪的風險管理。
因此，資訊安全的終點不是「修好問題」，而是讓整個系統變得更可靠。
二、Risk Management：如何知道哪些漏洞最值得先修？
1. 先從四個重要名詞開始
假設你是一間醫院的資訊安全工程師。

rows: 病歷資料夾權限設定錯誤
可能發生的損害及其可能性
私人病歷外洩，造成患者權益受損

sourceBody.text: 你要記住其中的因果關係：
有弱點，不代表有人利用；有人利用，也不代表每次都造成相同程度的損失。
例如，你發現兩個資料夾的權限都設錯了。
第一個放的是公開活動海報，第二個放的是患者的私人病歷。
雖然技術上的設定錯誤相同，但是潛在損害差異很大。
這就是風險管理不能只看漏洞數量的原因。
SVG 圖解 ②｜風險評估矩陣與四種處置方法

sourceBody.alt: 風險評估與四種處置方向。案例 A：公開活動海報：資料原本對外公開。示意為可能性中、影響低；仍須檢查其他存取與完整性問題。 案例 B：客戶私人文件：同樣的設定可能造成隱私、法遵與信任損害。示意為可能性中、影響高。 降低 Mitigate：修正共享權限、增加檢測並重新驗證。 避免 Avoid：取消不必要的公開分享功能，也可能犧牲便利性。 移轉／分擔 Transfer / Share：以契約或保險分配部分損失，不代表法定責任全部消失。 接受 Accept：由有權責的人理解風險後決定，留下理由與複查時間；不得逃避法律義務。 殘餘風險 Residual Risk：修好權限仍須確認先前存取與其他缺口；風險不一定歸零。
sourceBody.caption: 風險評估與四種處置方向｜原始 SVG，圖中文字維持原樣。

sourceBody.text: 2. 如何評估風險？
初學者可以先使用一個簡化模型：
Risk ≈ Likelihood × Impact
也就是：
風險 ≈ 發生可能性 × 影響程度
假設我們用 1～5 分評估兩個問題：

rows: 公開海報被未授權下載
私人病歷被未授權下載

sourceBody.text: 這個例子讓我們看到：
即使發生可能性相同，資料的重要程度不同，也會讓風險優先順序改變。
但請注意：這只是教學用的簡化評分方法，不是 NIST 規定所有組織都必須使用的公式。實務上還要考慮系統暴露程度、威脅能力、現有安全控制及評估的不確定性。
3. 發現風險後，只有「修補」這一種選擇嗎？
不是。
NIST 將風險回應整理成接受、避免、降低、分擔與移轉等方式。[NIST Computer Security Resource Center](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/risk_response)
我們用醫院的例子來理解。
Mitigate（降低風險）
醫院發現病歷資料夾權限設錯，因此重新設定權限，增加多因素驗證（MFA），並監控異常下載。
這些措施可以降低風險，但不能保證風險完全消失。
Avoid（避免風險）
醫院原本計畫建立一個不必要的公開病歷下載功能。評估後發現風險過高，決定取消這項功能。
這樣可以避免該功能引入的特定風險，但代價是失去部分便利性。
Transfer／Share（移轉／分擔風險）
醫院購買資安保險，並與外部服務供應商約定事故責任分工。
這可以分擔部分經濟損失，但醫院仍然必須履行自己的資安與法定責任。
Accept（接受風險）
有一個內部舊系統暫時無法升級。經過評估，負責人決定在特定期限內接受其殘餘風險，並採取其他補償性控制措施。
但接受風險必須有適當授權與紀錄，且不能用來逃避法律義務。
4. Residual Risk（殘餘風險）是什麼？
假設醫院已經修正病歷資料夾權限。
現在未授權存取的可能性降低了。
然而，還有兩個問題：
第一，修正之前，是否已經有人下載過資料？
第二，現在的權限設定是否仍可能受到其他安全問題影響？
這些尚未消除的風險，就是殘餘風險。
補充查證：殘餘風險是採取控制後仍存在的風險。「先前是否已被下載」是待查證的事件事實；若已有副本流出，修正權限仍無法消除其後續被使用或散布的風險。[NIST residual risk](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/residual_risk)
CEH 考試記憶重點：
Vulnerability Severity（漏洞嚴重度）不等於 Risk Level（風險等級）；修補完成也不代表 Residual Risk（殘餘風險）為零。
三、Incident Response：看到資安警報，應該怎麼辦？
先記住一個重要觀念：
資安工程師的責任不是立刻認定有人入侵，而是根據證據判斷發生了什麼事，再採取適當措施。
1. Event、Alert、Incident 有什麼不同？
假設某個醫院員工帳號，在凌晨兩點下載了 500 份病歷。
這時候，我們要區分三個概念。

rows: 監控工具認為這個行為值得注意
經分析，判定或合理懷疑涉及資安危害，需要依程序處理

sourceBody.text: 可能出現兩種情況。
情況 A：合法備份
經過調查，發現這個帳號是經過授權的備份服務帳號，每天凌晨都會執行備份。
因此，大量下載可能是正常工作。
情況 B：未授權存取
調查發現，下載者使用了已離職員工的帳號，而且該帳號不應該繼續擁有病歷存取權限。
這時就有充分理由啟動相應的資安事件處理程序。
注意：我們需要證據支持判斷，而不是依靠想像。
SVG 圖解 ③｜從告警到事件應變的完整流程

sourceBody.alt: 從告警到事件應變。觀察與告警 Event / Alert：系統記錄大量下載並發出通知：先區分觀察事實與需要查證的推測。 查證 Triage：比對身分與權限、時間與來源、資料內容、業務核准，以及原始日誌的完整性與時間一致性。 依證據判定：合理且已授權：記錄理由；證據不足：保留紀錄並補查；疑似或確認事件：依分級程序啟動應變。 證據保全與圍堵：依程序保存紀錄並限制損害，不是一律先關機或刪檔；兼顧服務與病人安全。 根除與復原：處理已確認原因與受影響元件，驗證服務可靠且可用。 改善與並行義務：檢查流程缺口、更新控制；通知義務、法遵與服務衝擊要並行評估。
sourceBody.caption: 從告警到事件應變｜原始 SVG，圖中文字維持原樣。

sourceBody.text: 2. 如果確認發生資安事件，接下來呢？
最容易混淆的三個動作是：
Containment（圍堵）
目的是防止傷害繼續擴大。
例如：確認某帳號遭到入侵後，依事件處理程序限制該帳號存取病歷系統。
這個動作不一定能解決入侵的根本原因，但可以減少持續損害。
Eradication（根除）
目的是處理已確認的入侵原因或惡意項目。
例如：確認攻擊者利用尚未修補的系統弱點取得存取權限，便需要修補弱點、處理被入侵的帳號及其他受影響元件。
Recovery（復原）
目的是讓系統回到可靠、可正常使用的狀態。
例如：確認帳號權限已恢復正確，病歷系統可以正常提供服務，且沒有發現未解決的惡意活動。
這三個動作的差別，可以用火災來記憶：

rows: 撲滅火源並處理引發火災的原因
確認安全後恢復建築物的正常使用

sourceBody.text: 重要取捨（Trade-off）
如果醫院的病歷系統遭到攻擊，立即關閉整套系統或許能阻止部分攻擊行為，但也可能讓急診醫師無法取得必要資訊。
因此，事件處理必須同時衡量：
安全風險、證據保全、服務可用性，以及病人的安全。
不是每次都應該直接關機、刪除檔案或全面中斷網路。
3. NIST SP 800-61 的新舊版本差異
這裡是 CEH 學習時需要特別留意的地方。
舊版 NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 常用四個階段說明事件應變：
Preparation → Detection & Analysis → Containment, Eradication & Recovery → Post-Incident Activity
這個模型仍然適合初學者理解事件處理的工作。
不過，NIST 已於 2025 年 4 月 3 日正式發布 SP 800-61 Rev. 3，取代 Rev. 2。

新版將事件應變整合進 NIST CSF 2.0：Govern、Identify、Protect 等活動提供平時的風險管理與準備；Detect、Respond、Recover 則構成新版事件應變生命週期的核心，並透過持續改善回饋組織。[NIST Computer Security Resource Center](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/incident-response)
因此：
舊版四階段可以幫助理解工作流程；新版則更強調事件應變與整體風險管理的整合。
遇到 CEH 考題時，應辨認題目採用的模型與版本。
四、NIST CSF 2.0：如何用一張地圖管理整間公司的資安？
我們已經知道如何評估風險，也知道遇到事件時如何處理。
但如果你是醫院的資訊長，應該如何確認整個組織的資安管理是否完整？
這就是 NIST Cybersecurity Framework（CSF，資安框架）能發揮作用的地方。
SVG 圖解 ④｜NIST CSF 2.0 六大功能與法遵架構

sourceBody.alt: CSF 2.0 與法遵地圖。Govern 治理：策略、責任、政策、風險容忍度與監督。 Identify 識別：盤點資產，辨認並評估風險。 Protect 保護：控制存取與權限，降低事件發生機會與影響。 Detect 偵測：觀察異常，產生可查證的訊號。 Respond 回應：判定事件，協調處置並限制損害。 Recover 復原：恢復重要服務，確認可靠且可用。 法律／法規：依適用條件履行法定義務，例如個資法、針對特定對象的資安法。 標準／產業要求：ISO/IEC 27001 管理系統、PCI DSS 支付卡資料安全；契約或法規可能使其成為義務。 框架 Framework：NIST CSF 2.0 協助盤點能力、目標與缺口。 內部政策／程序：寫清楚授權、責任、事件升級與通報方式。通過驗證不等於不會發生事件。
sourceBody.caption: CSF 2.0 與法遵地圖｜原始 SVG，圖中文字維持原樣。

sourceBody.text: 1. 六大功能如何理解？

rows: 誰負責資安？誰能做風險決定？
我們有哪些資產與風險？
如何防止問題發生或減少傷害？
發現事件後應如何處理？
如何讓受影響的服務恢復正常？

sourceBody.text: NIST CSF 2.0 於 2024 年發布，將 Govern 加入核心功能，從舊版五大功能擴充為六大功能。六個功能並不是必須依照順序完成的六個步驟，而是組織持續運作的資安管理面向。[NIST](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework/faqs)
2. 為什麼 Govern 特別重要？
想像你是一間醫院的資安工程師。
你發現某個病歷系統有高風險弱點。
但是修補系統需要停機兩個小時，可能影響醫療服務。
這時候，單靠工程技術無法決定一切。
你還需要知道：
誰有權批准停機？哪些醫療服務不能中斷？是否有替代作業方式？誰負責接受修補前的風險？
這些都是 Govern（治理）必須處理的問題。
治理並不只是管理階層簽文件，而是建立清楚的責任、決策權限與監督機制。
五、法律、標準、框架：有什麼不同？
這是 CEH 很容易混淆的概念。
我們用醫院來理解四種不同的要求。

rows: 適用時必須遵守的法定要求
協助整理管理目標與能力
組織自己訂定的規則與作業方式
病歷存取政策、事件通報 SOP

sourceBody.text: 但這不是絕對互斥的分類。例如，原本屬於標準的要求，也可能因為法律、契約或採購條件而成為特定組織必須履行的義務。
1. ISO/IEC 27001 到底在驗證什麼？
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 是資訊安全管理系統（Information Security Management System，ISMS）的國際標準。
它關注的不是單一防火牆或單一軟體，而是組織有沒有建立、實施、維持及持續改善資訊安全管理制度。[ISO](https://www.iso.org/standard/27001)
例如一家醫院可能需要證明自己有制度化地管理：
資產、資訊安全風險、人員責任、存取權限、事件處理，以及持續改善措施。
但要特別注意：
通過 ISO/IEC 27001 驗證，不等於每一套系統都沒有漏洞。
驗證有其適用範圍，而且管理制度有效運作，也不代表資安事件永遠不會發生。
2. PCI DSS 是什麼？
PCI DSS 全名為 Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard。
這是一套聚焦支付卡帳戶資料安全的產業標準。
例如醫院提供信用卡繳費功能，就可能需要評估相關支付系統與服務供應商的 PCI DSS 適用範圍。
它不只涉及直接儲存卡號的系統，也可能包含能影響持卡人資料環境安全的服務。[PCI Security Standards Council](https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/standards/pci-dss/)
因此，不能只因為付款服務已委外，就直接假設醫院完全沒有相關責任。
3. 臺灣的資安法律呢？
以臺灣為例，可以先認識兩項法律。
《個人資料保護法》主要規範個人資料的蒐集、處理與利用，並涉及相關保護義務。值得注意的是，2025 年修正的部分條文有尚未生效的情況，必須依查詢時實際施行的條文判斷。[National Legal Database](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?PCode=I0050021)
補充查證（2026-10-29）：全國法規資料庫仍標示部分修正條文尚未施行，應同時核對生效狀態與已施行條文。[個人資料保護法](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?PCode=I0050021)
《資通安全管理法》則針對公務機關與法律規定的特定非公務機關建立相關資安管理要求，不能直接假設所有民間企業都屬於相同的適用範圍。[law.moda.gov.tw](https://law.moda.gov.tw/LawContent.aspx?id=FL088622)
補充查證：2025-09-24 修正公布的資通安全管理法全文 35 條，已於 2025-12-01 施行；義務仍須依組織是否屬法定適用對象判定。[數發部法規沿革](https://law.moda.gov.tw/LawContentSource.aspx?id=FL088622)
這裡最重要的學習觀念不是背誦所有法條，而是建立一套判斷方式：
先確認組織、資料、業務活動與所在地，再確認適用法律、契約、標準及通報義務。
六、Information Assurance：資訊保證是什麼？
在 M01-01，我們已經學過 CIA Triad：
Confidentiality（機密性）、Integrity（完整性）、Availability（可用性）。
Information Assurance（資訊保證）除了這些資訊安全目標，也涵蓋身分驗證（Authentication）與不可否認性（Non-repudiation）等概念。[NIST Computer Security Resource Center](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/information_assurance)
我們可以用電子病歷簽署來理解。
醫師簽署一份電子病歷時，系統可能需要確認使用者身分、確保內容沒有遭到未授權更改，並留下可以查核的簽署證據。
不可否認性不是指任何人都絕對無法否認自己的行為，而是指系統能提供適當的技術證據，協助確認行為或資料來源。
例如數位簽章可以用來驗證資料的完整性與簽署來源，但實際爭議仍需要考慮金鑰管理及其他證據。
七、完整實戰案例：Northstar 平台出現大量下載
假設你加入一家名為 Northstar 的公司，擔任初階資安工程師。
公司提供客戶儲存私人文件的服務。
某天上午，你收到以下告警：
帳號 user017 在十分鐘內下載了 450 份文件，超過平常的使用量。
這是虛構教學情境。
第一個問題：這是否已經構成資安事件？
現在還不能確定。
我們只知道系統觀察到大量下載，而且監控工具產生告警。
你需要調查這個帳號是否具有存取權限、下載內容為何，以及操作是否符合正常業務情況。
第二個問題：如何整理證據？
建議建立三欄紀錄。

rows: user017 在十分鐘內下載 450 份文件
是否涉及未授權帳號存取？
交由指定人員判定事件等級
資料是否包含私人資訊？
確認是否需要採取限制措施

sourceBody.text: 這個方法的重要價值在於：
把事實、推測與決策分開，避免資安團隊在證據不足時過早下結論。
第三個問題：AI 可以提供什麼協助？
假設你使用 AI 協助整理事件資料。
AI 可以把不同來源的紀錄整理成時間線，協助比較異常行為，並摘要可能需要進一步查證的問題。
但不應該只因為 AI 回答「這是高風險事件」，就直接宣告資料外洩。
模型可能誤解時間、混淆不同帳號，甚至補出原始紀錄中不存在的細節。
因此，必須回查原始日誌，保留證據來源，並遵守組織對機敏資料與 AI 工具的使用規範。
第四個問題：事件處理完畢後呢？
假設最後證實某個離職員工的帳號沒有正確停用。
你修正了帳號權限，也確認不正常的存取行為已停止。
接下來還需要調查：
為什麼離職流程沒有停用帳號？其他離職帳號是否也存在類似問題？未來要如何自動檢查？
這些改善措施會重新進入風險管理流程。
從這裡就可以看出：
真正成熟的資安工作，不只是修好受影響的帳號，而是消除流程缺口，降低同類事件再次發生的可能性。
八、CEH M01-07 考前重點整理
這一課建議優先熟悉以下觀念：

rows: 降低、避免、分擔／移轉、接受
偵測、分析、圍堵、根除、復原
法律、標準、框架的定位與適用範圍

sourceBody.text: 星等是本課依基礎性、常見考題情境及跨章節重要性所做的教學排序，並非 EC-Council 公布的正式配分比例。
從整個 CEH M01 的角度，現在可以把已學過的內容串成一條完整主線：
CIA 安全目標 → 資產、威脅與弱點 → 合法授權 → 攻擊面 → 攻擊行為模型 → 安全控制 → 風險管理與事件應變。
這條主線就是你在後續 M02～M20 學習各種攻擊與防護技術時，可以反覆使用的概念地圖。
SVG 圖解下載
四張圖均為可縮放的 SVG 向量圖，適合放大閱讀、列印或匯入支援 SVG 的繪圖工具。
出版校訂：本次收到四張 SVG，請使用各圖下方的下載連結；主稿所述 ZIP 與 PNG 套件未提供，因此不列為可下載檔案。
九、理解檢核：用一個案例確認是否真的理解
請先不要查答案，試著用自己的話回答。
情境：
某醫院已通過 ISO/IEC 27001 相關驗證。
某天，醫院的資安系統發現一個帳號在凌晨大量下載患者病歷。
資訊主管說：
「我們已經通過 ISO/IEC 27001 驗證，所以應該不可能發生資安事件。把這個告警關閉就好了，不需要再調查。」
請回答以下四題：
1. 風險管理： 這個情境中的 Asset、Threat、Vulnerability、Risk 分別可能是什麼？哪些只是尚待查證的假設？
2. 事件應變： 為什麼不能只憑大量下載就宣告資料外洩？你會優先取得哪兩類證據？
3. 法律與標準： 為什麼醫院通過 ISO/IEC 27001 驗證，不代表一定沒有發生資安事件？是否需要通報，應如何判定？
4. NIST CSF： 如果最後確認是離職員工帳號未停用，你會如何運用 Identify、Protect、Detect、Respond、Recover 與 Govern，改善整個事件處理與管理制度？
這四題能檢查你是否已把 M01-07 的三個主要領域整合起來。 你回答後，我會逐題評估，指出已經理解的部分、推理上的缺口，以及 CEH 考題可能如何改變情境來測試相同觀念。

sourceBody.summary: 問題 1 參考解答｜風險管理：先把已知與假設分開
paragraphs: Asset 是病歷資料及相關服務。可能的 Threat 是未授權讀取；可能的 Vulnerability 是離職帳號未停用或權限過寬，但題目還沒有證實。Risk 是未授權存取造成隱私、服務及信任損害的可能性與影響。大量下載是觀察，不是直接證實弱點或外洩。

sourceBody.summary: 問題 2 參考解答｜事件應變：先查授權，再查實際活動
paragraphs: 大量下載也可能是合法備份。優先核對兩類證據：一是帳號身分、權限與業務核准紀錄；二是原始存取／下載日誌（時間、來源、資料範圍與結果）。必要時依程序保全證據、採取比例適當的圍堵，不必等完全確定才處理合理懷疑。

sourceBody.summary: 問題 3 參考解答｜法律與標準：通過驗證不代表永遠安全
paragraphs: ISO/IEC 27001 驗證有特定範圍，關注管理制度，不能保證每個系統零漏洞。通報要依組織、資料、事件事實、適用法規與契約、法定門檻及期限判斷，由指定權責人員處理，不能單憑「有驗證」或「有告警」決定。

sourceBody.summary: 問題 4 參考解答｜CSF：不是只停用一個帳號
paragraphs: Identify 盤點資產與離職帳號；Protect 改善停權與最小權限；Detect 偵測異常下載；Respond 調查、圍堵與協調通報；Recover 驗證服務與資料可靠性；Govern 決定責任、風險接受與監督制度。這些面向會相互回饋，不是只能照順序做一次。

sourceBody.text: 參考答案是補充教材，公布答案不代表讀者已作答或已理解。只在合法授權範圍內進行案例演練。

en.summary: Connect risk management, incident response and compliance into a continuous decision cycle; distinguish facts, hypotheses and accountability through concrete examples.

sourceBody.text: Risk Management · Incident Response · Laws & Standards
Module 01: Introduction to Ethical Hacking
This is the final learning unit in CEH M01. We will connect the knowledge from the previous six lessons to understand how an organization actually manages information security.
1. Start with the big picture: information security is an ongoing management system
The most important conclusion in this lesson is:

Security is not simply patching every vulnerability you find or dismissing every alert that appears. It means continually assessing risk, taking action, verifying results, and improving the next decision.
Think of the lesson as three questions:

rows: Decide how to prevent harm before something happens
Investigate and respond when something may already have happened
What happened, and how can we prevent further harm?
Establish the rules, responsibilities, and applicable requirements
What must we comply with, and who is accountable?

sourceBody.text: Verification note: this introductory table starts with prevention. Risk assessment also continues during and after an incident, not only before the next one. [NIST Incident Response](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/incident-response)
Another idea runs throughout all three:
Continuous Improvement means using the lessons from each inspection, exercise, and incident to improve future protection and management.
The following four SVG diagrams gradually explain how these ideas connect.
SVG diagram ① | The complete security-management decision cycle

sourceBody.alt: The security-management decision cycle。Risk Management：Identify important assets and threats; assess likelihood, impact and existing controls; set priorities and review dates. Incident Response：Check alerts against original evidence. Contain harm, address causes and verify recovery within authorization; do not close a case on guesses. Continuous Improvement：Find detection and process gaps; update access, procedures, exercises and training. Return to risk management：Use lessons learned to reassess residual risk. Fixing one vulnerability does not manage every risk; closing an alert does not prove safety.
sourceBody.caption: The security-management decision cycle | Original SVG; Chinese text inside the supplied image is unchanged.
sourceBody.openLabel: Open the original image to zoom

sourceBody.text: Follow the arrows in the diagram:
Risk management → Incident response → Improve governance → Return to risk management.
For example, a hospital discovers a security problem in its medical-record system.

During normal operations, the security team assesses the risk of medical records being exposed and establishes access controls. If an unusually large download occurs one day, the team must investigate whether unauthorized access is involved.
The work does not end when the incident has been handled.
The team must also ask: Why did the existing access controls fail to prevent the problem? Was detection too slow? Should the management process change?
Those answers inform the next round of risk management.
The endpoint of security work is therefore not merely “fixing the problem,” but making the overall system more reliable.
2. Risk Management: how do you decide which vulnerabilities to fix first?
1. Start with four important terms
Imagine that you are an information-security engineer at a hospital.

rows: Incorrect permissions on a medical-record folder
Private medical records are exposed, harming patients' rights and interests

sourceBody.text: Remember the causal relationship:
A weakness does not mean that someone has exploited it; exploitation does not mean that every occurrence causes the same amount of harm.
Suppose you find incorrect permissions on two folders.
The first contains public event posters. The second contains patients' private medical records.
Although the technical configuration error is the same, the potential harm is very different.
That is why risk management cannot consider only the number of vulnerabilities.
SVG diagram ② | A risk-assessment matrix and four ways to respond

sourceBody.alt: Risk assessment and four response directions。Case A: public event posters：The information was intended for public access: medium likelihood, low impact in this illustration. Still check other access and integrity concerns. Case B: private customer files：The same error may harm privacy, compliance and trust: medium likelihood, high impact in this illustration. Mitigate：Correct sharing permissions, add detection and verify again. Avoid：Cancel an unnecessary public-sharing feature, possibly sacrificing convenience. Transfer / Share：Allocate some losses through contracts or insurance; legal responsibilities do not simply disappear. Accept：An authorized accountable owner understands the risk and records reasons and a review date. Acceptance cannot evade law. Residual Risk：Check earlier access and remaining gaps after fixing permissions. Risk need not become zero.
sourceBody.caption: Risk assessment and four response directions | Original SVG; Chinese text inside the supplied image is unchanged.
sourceBody.openLabel: Open the original image to zoom

sourceBody.text: 2. How do we assess risk?
Beginners can start with a simplified model:
Risk ≈ Likelihood × Impact
In other words:
Risk ≈ likelihood of occurrence × severity of impact
Suppose we assess two issues using scores from 1 to 5:

rows: Unauthorized downloading of private medical records

sourceBody.text: The example shows that:
Even with the same likelihood, differences in the importance of the information can change risk priorities.

However, this is only a simplified teaching method—not a formula that NIST requires every organization to use. In practice, we must also consider system exposure, threat capabilities, existing security controls, and uncertainty in the assessment.
3. Is “patch it” the only option after identifying a risk?
No.
NIST describes risk responses including acceptance, avoidance, mitigation, sharing, and transfer. [NIST Computer Security Resource Center](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/risk_response)
Consider these hospital examples.
Mitigate
The hospital discovers incorrect permissions on a medical-record folder. It corrects the permissions, adds multifactor authentication (MFA), and monitors unusual downloads.
These measures can reduce risk, but cannot guarantee that all risk disappears.
Avoid
The hospital had planned an unnecessary feature for publicly downloading medical records. After assessing the excessive risk, it cancels the feature.
This avoids the particular risk introduced by that feature, at the cost of some convenience.
Transfer / Share
The hospital purchases cyber insurance and agrees on incident responsibilities with an external service provider.
This may share some financial losses, but the hospital must still fulfill its own security and legal responsibilities.
Accept
An old internal system cannot be upgraded immediately. Following an assessment, the responsible decision-maker accepts the residual risk for a defined period and applies other compensating controls.
Risk acceptance requires appropriate authorization and records; it cannot be used to evade legal obligations.
4. What is Residual Risk?
Suppose the hospital has corrected the medical-record folder's permissions.
The likelihood of unauthorized access has now decreased.
However, two questions remain:
First, did anyone download the information before the correction?
Second, could other security problems still affect the current permission arrangement?
The risk that has not been eliminated is residual risk.

Verification note: residual risk remains after controls are applied. Whether an earlier download occurred is an incident fact to verify; if copies escaped, changing permissions does not eliminate the risk of their later use or distribution. [NIST residual risk](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/residual_risk)
CEH exam memory point:
Vulnerability Severity is not the same as Risk Level; completing a patch does not mean that Residual Risk is zero.
3. Incident Response: what should you do when a security alert appears?
Start with an important idea:
A security engineer's job is not to immediately declare that an intrusion has occurred. It is to determine what happened from the evidence, then take appropriate action.
1. How do Event, Alert, and Incident differ?
Suppose a hospital employee account downloads 500 medical records at 2 a.m.
We must distinguish three ideas.

rows: An observed activity or event record
The system observes a large download
A monitoring tool considers the behavior worth attention
Analysis establishes or reasonably suspects a security harm that must be handled through the relevant process

sourceBody.text: There are two possible situations.
Situation A: authorized backup
Investigation finds that the account is an authorized backup service account that runs a backup every early morning.
The large download may therefore be normal work.
Situation B: unauthorized access
Investigation finds that the downloader used a former employee's account, which should no longer have access to medical records.
There is now sufficient reason to initiate the appropriate security-incident handling procedure.
Our judgment needs evidence, not imagination.
SVG diagram ③ | The complete path from alert to incident response

sourceBody.alt: From an alert to incident response。Event / Alert：A system records bulk downloads and issues a notification. Separate observations from hypotheses. Triage：Check identity and permissions, time and origin, data content, business approval, and the completeness and time consistency of original logs. Evidence-based decision：Authorized and reasonable: record why. Insufficient evidence: preserve records and investigate. Suspected or confirmed incident: activate the appropriate response procedure. Preserve evidence and contain：Preserve records and limit harm under procedure; do not automatically power off or delete files. Consider service and patient safety. Eradicate and recover：Address confirmed causes and affected components; verify that services are trustworthy and available. Improve and meet parallel obligations：Fix process gaps and update controls. Assess notification duties, compliance and service impact in parallel.
sourceBody.caption: From an alert to incident response | Original SVG; Chinese text inside the supplied image is unchanged.
sourceBody.openLabel: Open the original image to zoom

sourceBody.text: 2. What happens after a security incident is confirmed?
Three actions are particularly easy to confuse:
Containment
The aim is to prevent further harm.
For example, after confirming that an account is compromised, restrict its access to the medical-record system according to the incident-handling procedure.
This may not address the root cause of the intrusion, but it can reduce continuing harm.
Eradication
The aim is to address confirmed causes of the intrusion or malicious components.
For example, if evidence confirms that an attacker gained access through an unpatched weakness, patch that weakness and address compromised accounts and other affected components.
Recovery
The aim is to restore the system to a trustworthy, usable state.
For example, verify that account permissions are correct again, the medical-record system can provide normal services, and no unresolved malicious activity has been found.
A fire analogy can help you remember the difference:

rows: First prevent the fire from spreading
Extinguish the source and address the cause of the fire
Restore normal use of the building after verifying safety

sourceBody.text: An important trade-off

If a hospital's medical-record system is attacked, immediately shutting down the entire system might stop some attack activity—but could also prevent emergency physicians from accessing necessary information.
Incident handling must therefore weigh all of the following:
Security risk, evidence preservation, service availability, and patient safety.
Shutting down equipment, deleting files, or disconnecting the entire network is not always the appropriate response.
3. Differences between the old and new NIST SP 800-61 versions
This is an important point to watch when studying CEH.
The older NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 commonly explains incident response in four phases:
Preparation → Detection & Analysis → Containment, Eradication & Recovery → Post-Incident Activity
This model remains useful for helping beginners understand incident-handling work.
However, NIST formally published SP 800-61 Rev. 3 on April 3, 2025, replacing Rev. 2.

The new revision integrates incident response into NIST CSF 2.0. Activities under Govern, Identify, and Protect support everyday risk management and preparation; Detect, Respond, and Recover form the core of the new incident-response life cycle, with continuous improvement feeding lessons back into the organization. [NIST Computer Security Resource Center](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/incident-response)
Therefore:
The older four phases help explain the work process; the newer model places greater emphasis on integrating incident response with overall risk management.
When answering a CEH question, identify the model and version used in that question.
4. NIST CSF 2.0: how can one map help manage an organization's security?
We now know how to assess risk and how to handle incidents.
But if you were a hospital's chief information officer, how would you check whether security management across the organization was complete?
This is where the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) can help.
SVG diagram ④ | The six NIST CSF 2.0 functions and the compliance landscape

sourceBody.alt: CSF 2.0 and the compliance map。Govern：Strategy, accountability, policy, risk tolerance and oversight. Identify：Inventory assets and identify and assess risks. Protect：Manage access and permissions; reduce incident likelihood and impact. Detect：Observe anomalies and produce signals that can be investigated. Respond：Determine incidents, coordinate action and limit harm. Recover：Restore important services and verify trustworthiness and availability. Laws and regulations：Fulfil duties when statutory applicability conditions are met, such as privacy law and cybersecurity law for specified entities. Standards and industry requirements：ISO/IEC 27001 for management systems and PCI DSS for payment-card data. Contracts or law can make requirements binding. Framework：NIST CSF 2.0 helps identify capabilities, objectives and gaps. Internal policy and procedures：Specify authorization, responsibility, escalation and reporting. Certification does not guarantee that incidents cannot occur.
sourceBody.caption: CSF 2.0 and the compliance map | Original SVG; Chinese text inside the supplied image is unchanged.
sourceBody.openLabel: Open the original image to zoom

sourceBody.text: 1. How should we understand the six functions?

rows: Who is accountable for security, and who may make risk decisions?
What assets and risks do we have?
How do we prevent problems or reduce harm?
How do we discover possible anomalies?
How should we handle an incident once it is discovered?
How do we restore affected services to normal operation?

sourceBody.text: Published in 2024, NIST CSF 2.0 added Govern to the core functions, expanding the previous five to six. These functions are not six steps that must be completed in order; they are ongoing aspects of organizational security management. [NIST](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework/faqs)
2. Why is Govern especially important?
Imagine that you are a hospital security engineer.
You discover a high-risk weakness in a medical-record system.
However, patching it requires two hours of downtime and could affect medical services.
Technical expertise alone cannot decide everything.
You also need to know:
Who may approve the downtime? Which medical services cannot be interrupted? Are alternative operating arrangements available? Who is responsible for accepting the risk before the patch is applied?
These are all questions for Govern.
Governance is not merely management signing documents. It establishes clear accountability, decision-making authority, and oversight.
5. Laws, standards, and frameworks: what is the difference?
These concepts are easily confused in CEH.
Use a hospital to understand four different types of requirements.

rows: Statutory requirements that must be followed when applicable
Structures for organizing management objectives and capabilities
An organization's own rules and operating methods
Medical-record access policy and an incident-reporting SOP

sourceBody.text: These categories are not entirely mutually exclusive. For example, a standard's requirements may become binding for a particular organization through legislation, contracts, or procurement conditions.
1. What does ISO/IEC 27001 certification actually assess?
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 is the international standard for an Information Security Management System (ISMS).

Its focus is not a single firewall or software product. It concerns whether an organization has established, implemented, maintained, and continually improved an information-security management system. [ISO](https://www.iso.org/standard/27001)
For example, a hospital might need to demonstrate systematic management of:
Assets, information-security risks, personnel responsibilities, access rights, incident handling, and continual improvement measures.
But remember:
ISO/IEC 27001 certification does not mean that every system is free of vulnerabilities.
Certification has a defined scope. Even an effectively operating management system does not mean that security incidents can never occur.
2. What is PCI DSS?
PCI DSS stands for Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard.
It is an industry standard focused on payment-card account-data security.
For example, a hospital that accepts credit-card payments may need to assess the PCI DSS scope of its payment systems and service providers.

The scope is not limited to systems that directly store card numbers. It may include services that can affect the security of the cardholder data environment. [PCI Security Standards Council](https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/standards/pci-dss/)
Outsourcing payment services therefore does not automatically remove all of the hospital's responsibilities.
3. What about Taiwan's cybersecurity laws?
For Taiwan, begin by recognizing two laws.

The Personal Data Protection Act mainly governs the collection, processing, and use of personal data, including related protection obligations. Some provisions amended in 2025 have not yet taken effect; decisions must be based on the provisions actually in force when consulted. [National Legal Database](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?PCode=I0050021)

Verification note (2026-10-29): the official database still marks some amended provisions as not yet effective. Check commencement status as well as the provisions currently in force. [Personal Data Protection Act](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?PCode=I0050021)

The Cyber Security Management Act establishes relevant security-management requirements for government agencies and specified non-government agencies defined by law. Do not assume that all private businesses fall within the same scope. [Ministry of Digital Affairs legal database](https://law.moda.gov.tw/LawContent.aspx?id=FL088622)

Verification note: the 35-article revision promulgated on 2025-09-24 took effect on 2025-12-01. Duties still depend on whether the organization is a statutory covered entity. [MODA legislative history](https://law.moda.gov.tw/LawContentSource.aspx?id=FL088622)
The important learning goal is not memorizing every article of law, but developing a method of judgment:
First establish the organization, information, business activities, and location; then identify the applicable laws, contracts, standards, and reporting obligations.
6. Information Assurance: what does it mean?
In M01-01, we introduced the CIA Triad:
Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability.

In addition to these security objectives, Information Assurance encompasses concepts such as Authentication and Non-repudiation. [NIST Computer Security Resource Center](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/information_assurance)
Consider the signing of an electronic medical record.

When a physician signs a record, the system may need to establish the user's identity, ensure that the content has not been changed without authorization, and retain verifiable evidence of the signature.

Non-repudiation does not mean that it is absolutely impossible for someone to deny an action. It means that a system can provide appropriate technical evidence to help establish an action or a data source.
For example, a digital signature can help verify data integrity and the signing source, but an actual dispute still requires consideration of key management and other evidence.
7. A complete worked example: large downloads on the Northstar platform
Suppose you join a company called Northstar as a junior security engineer.
The company provides a service for customers to store private documents.
One morning, you receive this alert:
Account user017 downloaded 450 documents in ten minutes, exceeding its usual activity.
This is a fictional teaching scenario.
First question: is this already a security incident?
We cannot determine that yet.
We only know that the system observed a large download and the monitoring tool generated an alert.
You need to investigate whether the account was authorized, what it downloaded, and whether the activity fits normal business operations.
Second question: how should the evidence be organized?
Use a three-column record.

rows: user017 downloaded 450 documents in ten minutes
Was this an authorized batch download?
Preserve the relevant logs according to procedure
The download volume exceeded normal activity
Have the designated personnel determine incident severity
The system generated an anomaly alert
Did the data include private information?

sourceBody.text: The important benefit of this method is:
Separating facts, hypotheses, and decisions prevents the security team from reaching premature conclusions on insufficient evidence.
Third question: how can AI help?
Suppose you use AI to help organize incident information.
AI can arrange records from different sources into a timeline, help compare anomalous behavior, and summarize questions requiring further investigation.
But you should not declare a data breach simply because AI says, “This is a high-risk incident.”
A model may misunderstand timestamps, confuse different accounts, or even add details that do not exist in the original records.
Therefore, check the original logs, retain evidence provenance, and follow the organization's rules for sensitive information and AI tools.
Fourth question: what happens after the incident has been handled?
Suppose the investigation ultimately confirms that a former employee's account was not correctly disabled.
You correct its permissions and confirm that the abnormal access has stopped.
You still need to investigate:
Why did the departure process fail to disable the account? Do other former employees' accounts have the same problem? How can this be checked automatically in the future?
These improvements feed back into risk management.
This shows that:
Mature security work is not just fixing the affected account. It closes process gaps and reduces the likelihood of similar incidents recurring.
8. CEH M01-07 pre-exam review
Prioritize the following concepts in this lesson:

rows: Detection, analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery
Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, and Recover
The roles and applicability of laws, standards, and frameworks

CIA security objectives → Assets, threats, and vulnerabilities → Legal authorization → Attack surface → Models of attacker behavior → Security controls → Risk management and incident response.
This thread provides a conceptual map to revisit while learning attack and defense techniques in M02–M20.

9. Understanding check: use one scenario to test your understanding
Try answering in your own words before checking the answers.
Scenario:
A hospital has obtained relevant ISO/IEC 27001 certification.
One day, its security system discovers that an account downloaded a large number of patient records early in the morning.
The information manager says:
“We have ISO/IEC 27001 certification, so a security incident should be impossible. Just dismiss the alert; there is no need to investigate.”
Answer the following four questions:
1. Risk management: What might the Asset, Threat, Vulnerability, and Risk be in this scenario? Which are only hypotheses that still require verification?
2. Incident response: Why does a large download alone not establish a data breach? Which two types of evidence would you obtain first?
3. Laws and standards: Why does ISO/IEC 27001 certification not establish that no security incident occurred? How should reporting requirements be determined?

4. NIST CSF: If the investigation confirms that a former employee's account was not disabled, how would you use Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover, and Govern to improve the overall incident-handling process and management system?

These four questions check whether you can connect the three main areas of M01-07. After you answer, I can evaluate each response, identify what you understand and any gaps in reasoning, and explain how a CEH question might change the scenario to test the same ideas.

sourceBody.summary: Question 1: reference answer — Risk management: separate facts from hypotheses
paragraphs: Assets include patient records and related services. A possible threat is unauthorized access; a possible vulnerability is an active former-employee account or excessive permissions, neither yet established. Risk concerns the likelihood and impact of privacy, service and trust harm. Bulk downloading is an observation, not proof of a vulnerability or breach.

sourceBody.summary: Question 2: reference answer — Incident response: check authorization and actual activity
paragraphs: Bulk downloading can be an authorized backup. Prioritize identity, permission and business-approval records, plus original access/download logs covering time, origin, data scope and results. Preserve evidence and take proportionate containment under procedure; reasonable suspicion can require action before complete certainty.

sourceBody.summary: Question 3: reference answer — Law and standards: certification is not permanent safety
paragraphs: ISO/IEC 27001 certification has a defined scope and assesses a management system; it cannot guarantee zero vulnerabilities. Reporting depends on the organization, data, incident facts, applicable law and contracts, thresholds and deadlines. The designated accountable personnel must determine requirements, not infer them solely from certification or an alert.

sourceBody.summary: Question 4: reference answer — CSF: more than disabling one account
paragraphs: Identify assets and former-employee accounts; Protect through deprovisioning and least privilege; Detect unusual downloads; Respond through investigation, containment and reporting coordination; Recover by validating service and data reliability; Govern through accountability, risk acceptance and oversight. These areas inform one another rather than running only once in sequence.
